headline: Adaptive attacker search makes prompt-injection success rise with compute in two synthetic agent suites
summary: A September 3 preprint models indirect prompt injection as an attacker search problem and evaluates a GLM-5.2 attacker with environment reconnaissance, explicit strategy/history state and victim-feedback probes. In synthetic Workspace and Retail suites, the authors report that attack success rises as the attacker receives more test-time tokens: GPT-5.5 reaches 52.1% ASR at 100,000 tokens in Workspace, while Claude Opus 4.8 reaches 20.6% at 500,000 tokens in Retail. Removing the search harness causes gains to plateau after about 100,000 tokens, and removing explicit strategy management leads to repeated reconnaissance and attack patterns. The study is white-box, uses synthetic tasks and one attacker against two victims; black-box transfer and independent reproduction are not established.
